newsitem.title: USA: Calif. 1997 hydropower output seen exceeding 1995.
newsitem.headline: Calif. 1997 hydropower output seen exceeding 1995.

text.p: California's hydroelectric power output this year will likely exceed the volume seen in 1995, which was the state's highest since 1983, industry sources said Wednesday.
In 1995, according to the California Department of Finance, statewide hydroelectric generation totaled 51,665 gigawatt hours (GWh), or 145 percent of the long-term average.
Last year's output was about seven percent less than in 1995.
But this year's precipitation, snowpack and reservoir levels indicate hydropower output will total around 55,000 GWh in 1997, the California Energy Commission said.
According to the state's Department of Water Resources' early-February assessment, statewide runoff will total 195 percent of average levels for the water year of October 1996 to September 1997.

Precipitation between last October and early February was 185 percent of average levels, while snowpack was at 155 percent of normal and reservoir storage was 130 percent of average, the state agency said.
In 1995, hydropower accounted for 25 percent of the state's total power output, compared with 38 percent from natural gas-fired sources, Energy Commission statistics show.
In a much drier year, such as 1994, hydropower provided just 12 percent of California's total electricity generation, while gas-fired plants accounted for 44 percent.
